brief.subject: Ghana timber licensing in focus; Kraft Heinz exits US coffee
brief.headline: Ghana's EU Timber License Examined; Kraft Heinz Sells North American Coffee Unit
brief.dek: A look at Ghana's 16-year path to an EU timber licensing deal, plus a $650 million coffee divestment and new cocoa supply options.
brief.lede: It's a quiet day for EUDR news. The main item is a Mongabay analysis of how Ghana's EU timber partnership has strengthened forest governance and market access.

sections.heading: Ghana's EU timber deal under review
bullets: Ghana spent 16 years negotiating a Voluntary Partnership Agreement with the EU before reaching its licensing milestone last year.
Europe is a key buyer of Ghanaian timber, so legality credentials directly shape access for wood exporters.
Beyond market access, the VPA brought support for stronger national forest governance, which the analysis says improved cooperation.
Note that this is an analysis piece, so treat its conclusions as interpretation rather than confirmed outcomes.

sections.heading: Kraft Heinz sells coffee unit for $650M
bullets: Kraft Heinz is selling its North American coffee business to One Rock for $650 million.
Kraft Heinz will keep a 30% stake and use the cash to cut debt.
Coffee suppliers selling to this business should watch for a change in buyer ownership and possible shifts in sourcing contacts.

sections.heading: Cocoa alternatives gain ground
bullets: Fermentation, cocoa alternatives and cultured cacao are giving bakery and snack makers new options for flavour, formulation and supply.
Cocoa exporters should track these substitutes because they could change long-term demand from snack manufacturers.
